acceptance: All three prerequisite SSB tracker items (crr-c2-row-count-references-tpc-and-ssb, pvm-p1-run-ssb-clickbench, pvm-p2-publish-ssb-clickbench) are confirmed done before implementation starts.

Owner-approved Gate C acceptance report compares legacy vs new SSB column distributions, FK integrity across all 5 tables (date, customer, supplier, part, lineorder), and exact dual-engine DuckDB and DataFusion row-count agreement on all 13 SSB queries at SF 0.01, 0.1, 1.0, and 10.0.

benchbox/core/expected_results/ssb_results.py cleanly keys/versions v1 (legacy) and v2 (new) SSB_EXPECTED_ROW_COUNTS with frozen golden per-table hashes, and both legacy and native modes validate without cache collisions.

context: Owner decision A3 (2026-11-23): include SSB in scope via a versioned per-benchmark RNG and reference-count migration, explicitly gated after open SSB reference and Polars publication items close so active SSB corpus work is not disrupted.
description:
## Problem
benchbox/core/ssb/generator.py relies on single-threaded Python random.Random(42) loops, and benchbox/core/expected_results/ssb_results.py pins SSB_EXPECTED_ROW_COUNTS to that exact Python MT19937 stream. Changing SSB's RNG without per-benchmark versioning and sequencing after active SSB reference/publication items would break corpus comparability and in-flight SSB work.

## Change
- Once crr-c2-row-count-references-tpc-and-ssb, pvm-p1-run-ssb-clickbench, and pvm-p2-publish-ssb-clickbench are done, implement a vectorized Python/PyArrow SSB generator behind opt-in --datagen-backend native (following adr-python-core-runtime.md's vectorized-Python-first order).
- Assign an explicit per-benchmark SSB generator version in datagen_version.py (never bumping global DATA_GENERATION_VERSION) and keep legacy random.Random(42) available behind --datagen-backend legacy for reproducing v1 published results.
- Produce a Gate C owner acceptance report comparing legacy vs new SSB distributions, 0-orphan FK integrity across all 5 tables (date, customer, supplier, part, lineorder), and all 13 SSB query row counts at SF 0.01, 0.1, 1.0, and 10.0 on both DuckDB and DataFusion (requiring exact two-engine agreement).
- Update benchbox/core/expected_results/ssb_results.py so SSB_EXPECTED_ROW_COUNTS supports both v1 (legacy) and v2 (new) cleanly, and freeze golden per-table hashes.
- Measure wall time (mono_time()) and peak RSS under make heavy-run against SSB's Phase 0 ADR budget (Gate D).

## Decision gates
- Hard blocked on crr-c2-row-count-references-tpc-and-ssb, pvm-p1-run-ssb-clickbench, and pvm-p2-publish-ssb-clickbench closing first.
- Stop and report if DuckDB and DataFusion disagree on any of the 13 SSB queries at any recorded scale; never pick one engine arbitrarily.
- Owner must sign off on the Gate C acceptance report before merging.
- If vectorized Python SSB still misses its ADR budget at SF 1/SF 10, record the residual bottleneck and route SSB to datagen-p2-rust-repo-gate (or follow-up on the Rust repo).

## Guardrails
- Zero unversioned change to SSB data or SSB_EXPECTED_ROW_COUNTS.
- Never bump global DATA_GENERATION_VERSION.
- Enforce [RUN-DATA-001], [HEAVY-LOCK-001], [COMMENT-POLICY-001], and AGENTS.md PR closeout.
